title: Knuckle Boom Marine Cranes for Harbour Workboats in Egypt
seo_title: Knuckle Boom Marine Cranes on Egypt Workboats | BOB-LIFT
seo_description: How BOB-LIFT SQ5ZA3T 5-ton knuckle boom marine cranes were fitted to harbour workboats in Egypt, from shipyard outfitting to the finished boat on the water.
summary: Customer photos from Egypt follow BOB-LIFT SQ5ZA3T knuckle boom marine cranes from shipyard outfitting to a finished harbour workboat on the water.

sections.heading: Project at a glance
sections.body:
A customer in Egypt fitted BOB-LIFT SQ5ZA3T knuckle boom marine cranes to steel harbour workboats and sent back 14 photos of the job; nine of them are shown on this page. The set starts at the shipyard, where the bare hulls still carry primer and two yellow cranes are already standing on deck, and ends with a finished orange-red workboat, hull number SG1, running on open water under an Egyptian flag. Above the hull number, the Arabic lettering reads "Alexandria" (اسكندرية).

In order, the photos show:
1. Bare hulls in primer at the yard, with the cranes already on deck.
2. Each crane on a raised pedestal, with a seat control station and access ladder.
3. A hydraulic power unit housed on deck beside the crane.
4. The finished SG1 afloat, with the crane folded on the aft deck.

Everything below comes from those photos and the crane's spec sheet. Lift weights and operating hours were not shared, so they are not given here.

sections.heading: Why a knuckle boom crane suits a small workboat
sections.body:
A harbour workboat has little free deck. A knuckle boom folds into a compact package when it is not working, so it leaves the aft deck clear for mooring lines, fenders and cargo. When it is needed, the boom unfolds over the side or the stern and reaches further out over the side than a fixed davit.

The SQ5ZA3T is rated at 5,000 kg maximum lifting capacity and 10.5 t·m maximum lifting moment, with 360° slewing. The maximum capacity applies close to the column; the load chart reduces it as the radius grows, so the job, not the headline figure, should decide the size. At 2,060 kg self weight it adds a moderate deck load, but the vessel's designer should still check the deck structure and stability with the crane loaded at full outreach.

sections.heading: Outfitting at the yard
sections.body:
The yard photos show the cranes bolted to raised pedestals on the aft deck before the hull was painted. Each crane has a seat control station with its own access ladder, so the operator sits above the deck with a direct view of the load. The hydraulic hoses run in a bundle down the column, away from the working area.

One close-up shows an orange hydraulic power unit housed on deck next to the crane. Marine cranes like this need a hydraulic supply of the right flow and pressure; for the SQ5ZA3T that is 35 L/min at 28 MPa, from roughly 22 kW of recommended power, with a 100 L oil tank.

sections.heading: On the water
sections.body:
The last photos show the SG1 afloat and finished: orange-red hull, white wheelhouse, tyre fenders along the rail and the yellow crane folded on the aft deck. Folded, the crane sits low behind the wheelhouse, which is a main reason to choose a folding boom on a boat this size: where deck space is short, folded height matters more than maximum reach.

The full set of customer photos is on the SQ5ZA3T customer feedback page linked below.

sections.heading: Planning a similar marine crane
sections.body: If you are fitting a crane to a workboat, tug or service vessel, send us the deck layout, the heaviest load and the reach you need, and the hydraulic power available on board. We will match a model from the knuckle boom marine crane range, such as the 4-ton SQ4ZA3T or the 6.3-ton SQ6.3ZA5T, and check the load chart against your outreach. BOB-LIFT marine cranes are supplied without classification society certification, so tell us early if your vessel needs class approval.

title: Setting Utility Poles with a Truck-Mounted Crane in Honduras
seo_title: Truck-Mounted Crane for Utility Poles in Honduras | BOB-LIFT
seo_description: Customer photos from Honduras show a BOB-LIFT SQ6.3ZA4 truck-mounted knuckle boom crane unloading and setting utility poles on a power line job.
summary: A BOB-LIFT SQ6.3ZA4 truck-mounted knuckle boom crane unloads and stands utility poles for a power line crew in Honduras.

sections.heading: Project at a glance
sections.body:
A customer in Honduras mounted a BOB-LIFT SQ6.3ZA4 truck-mounted knuckle boom crane behind the cab of a white flatbed truck and used it on a power line job. The customer sent back 10 photos and a short video.

The job sequence they show:
1. Unload poles from the truck bed.
2. Swing them to the edge of the track and lay them out.
3. Stand each pole upright in a freshly dug hole while a crew in hi-vis guides the base.

What follows sticks to those photos and the crane's spec sheet. The customer did not share how many poles were set, so no such figure appears here.

sections.heading: Why a knuckle boom crane fits pole work
sections.body:
Pole setting asks a crane to do two different jobs on the same day. First it unloads long poles from the bed and lays them out; then it lifts each pole, normally slung above its centre of gravity, and holds it vertical while the crew backfills the hole. A knuckle boom does both from the truck: it reaches over the bed without a separate loader, and the hook can be placed precisely above the hole by folding and extending the boom rather than moving the truck.

When the job is done, the boom folds into the space behind the cab, so the truck keeps most of its bed for poles and a low transport height between jobs.

sections.heading: What the SQ6.3ZA4 is rated for
sections.body: The SQ6.3ZA4 is a 6.3-ton class crane: 6,300 kg maximum lifting capacity and 13.2 t·m maximum lifting moment, with 360° slewing. Its hydraulic system runs at 40 L/min and 28 MPa from about 22 kW of recommended power, with a 100 L oil tank, and the crane weighs 2,180 kg. As with every knuckle boom crane, the rated load drops with radius, so a long, heavy pole lifted at full reach needs checking against the load chart, not the maximum figure.

sections.heading: Outriggers on a gravel verge
sections.body:
In the photos the outrigger legs are lowered to the ground on both sides in the photos, including on loose gravel at the side of the track. Outriggers carry the overturning load into the ground instead of the truck's springs and tyres. On soft ground, add wide pads under the outrigger feet to spread the load further; it is a small item that makes a large difference when the crane holds a pole at reach.

On a power line job, the other limit is clearance. If poles go up next to energized lines, keep the minimum clearances set by your electrical utility and local regulations; the US OSHA rule for cranes near power lines, 29 CFR 1926.1408, is a widely used reference.

sections.heading: Planning a similar utility truck
sections.body: For pole and utility work, tell us the length and weight of your heaviest pole, the distance from the truck to the hole, and the truck chassis you plan to use. We will check the load chart at that radius and recommend a crane size and mounting position that leave enough payload for the poles.

title: Lifting Machinery and a Steel Tank with a 12-Ton Truck Crane in Argentina
seo_title: Truck Crane Lifts Tank and Machinery in Argentina | BOB-LIFT
seo_description: Customer photos from Argentina: a BOB-LIFT SQ12ZA4 knuckle boom truck crane sets a steel tank on its stand and moves machinery inside industrial sheds.
summary: A BOB-LIFT SQ12ZA4 12-ton knuckle boom truck crane lifts a steel tank onto its stand and moves wrapped machinery inside industrial sheds in Argentina.

sections.heading: Project at a glance
sections.body:
A customer in Argentina mounted a yellow BOB-LIFT SQ12ZA4 12-ton knuckle boom truck crane behind the cab of a rigid truck and sent back 11 photos of it at work. Outdoors, the crane lifts a round steel tank onto a raised steel stand next to a sheet-metal building. Indoors, the truck drives into large industrial sheds and the crane lifts long, plastic-wrapped machines off their skids while a small team steadies them by hand.

We only know what the pictures show and what the spec sheet says. The weights involved and the customer's line of business were not shared.

sections.heading: One truck for outdoor and indoor lifts
sections.body:
The photos show the same truck doing two quite different lifts: one outdoors at height, one indoors under a roof. Outside, the boom is raised high to clear the top of the stand and set the tank down on it. Inside, the boom is kept low and folded so it works under the roof trusses and next to an existing overhead crane whose beam is marked 2 t.

A knuckle boom makes this possible because its sections fold. The operator can bring the hook in close and low for indoor work, or unfold the boom to full height outdoors, without changing equipment.

sections.heading: What the SQ12ZA4 is rated for
sections.body:
In the BOB-LIFT model code, SQ12 is the 12-ton class, Z is a knuckle (folding) boom and A4 means one main boom plus three hydraulic extension booms. The SQ12ZA4 is rated at 12,000 kg maximum lifting capacity and 27 t·m maximum lifting moment, with 360° slewing. Recommended power is about 30 kW; the hydraulics run at 55 L/min and 28 MPa with a 160 L oil tank. The crane weighs 4,480 kg and needs 1,400 mm of installation space behind the cab.

The maximum capacity applies close to the column. Check the load chart at your real radius rather than the headline figure.

sections.heading: Setting up indoors
sections.body:
Each indoor set of photos shows the same routine:
1. Drive the truck into the shed.
2. Extend the yellow-and-black outrigger legs and lower them onto the concrete floor.
3. Rig slings and spreader straps to the machine skids.
4. Lift and lower the machine into position.

On a finished floor the outriggers matter twice: they keep the truck level and stable, and they spread the crane's load over a larger area of the slab; pads under the outrigger feet reduce point loads further. For indoor placement, plan the lift in advance; UK HSE guidance on LOLER is a widely used reference for lift planning. Tag lines give extra control of a suspended load and keep hands off it.

sections.heading: Planning a similar project
sections.body: If you move machinery into buildings or install tanks and silos, tell us the heaviest item, the radius from the truck, the clear height inside the building and the truck chassis you plan to use. We will check the load chart at that radius and recommend a crane size that fits under your roof and on your truck.
